question.problem:
Let $D$ be a finite region enclosed by the curve ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=1.$ If 

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y), & (x,y)\in R\cap D \\ 0, & (x,y)\in R∖D\end{aligned}\,\text{and}\,{∬}_{D}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)\,\text{d}A={∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A,
$$

which of the following could be the definition of the rectangular domain $R?$

I. $R=[-1,1]\times [-1,1]$

II. $R=[-1,1]\times [0,1]$

III. $R=[-2,2]\times [-2,2]$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's draw our region $D:$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14136443/assets/c50e0e01d432b1db736fad09dd5f5b82286e981d88586e848d9b57c8a9910eb0.png)

Notice that if $R$ covers $D$ completely and we define 

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y), & (x,y)\in R\cap D \\ 0, & (x,y)\in R∖D,\end{aligned}
$$

we obtain

$$
{∬}_{D}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)\,\text{d}A={∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

With that in mind, let's examine each of the given rectangles.

- Rectangle II does not cover the region $D.$

- Rectangles I and III covers the region $D$ completely.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."
